'''Wemba Wemba''' is an extinct [[Aboriginal Australian language]] once spoken along the [[Murray River]] and its tributaries in North Western [[Victoria (Australia)|Victoria]] and South Central [[New South Wales]].

Voiced consonant sounds only occur within prenasalized stops. Prenasal consonants include: /mb/ /nd/ /ndy/ /ng/ and /rnd/. In phonetic form they are pronounced as [mb] [nd] [ɲɟ] [ŋɡ] and [ɳɖ].<ref>{{Cite book|title=Wembawemba Dictionary|last=Hercus|first=Luise A.|year=1992}}</ref>

==Influence on English==
At least four botanical terms in [[Australian English]] are thought to have been introduced into local speech from Wemba-Wemba:
* {{Lang|xww|dilanj}} = [[Nitraria billardierei|nitre bush/dillon]]
* {{Lang|xww|lerep}} = [[Lerp (biology)|lerp/honeydew or lerp manna]]<ref name=clarke2008>{{cite book | last=Clarke | first=Philip A. | title=Aboriginal Plant Collectors: Botanists and Australian Aboriginal People in the Nineteenth Century | publisher=Rosenberg | year=2008 | isbn=978-1-877058-68-4 | url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Usav1CwZaXEC&pg=PA52 | access-date=25 May 2021 | page=52}}</ref>
* {{Lang|xww|gambang}} = [[Typha|bulrush/cumbungi]]<ref name=clarke2008/>
* {{Lang|xww|mali}} = [[Mallee (habit)|mallee]]<ref name=clarke2008/>
* The word [[Common yabby|yabby]], a type of [[crayfish]], comes from Wemba-Wemba.<ref>''[[Oxford Dictionary of English]]'', p 2,054.</ref>
